title: Rollforward-first CI/CD notes for private deploys: canary, TF modules, image provenance
content:
Context and goals:

This is an internal working draft capturing a rollforward-first CI/CD pattern for private deployments (VPC/on-prem). Focus is on safe progressive upgrades using Argo/GitOps+Helm, Terraform module versioning for infra + cluster provisioning, and cryptographic image provenance (cosign/Sigstore) tied into the CI pipeline.

Why rollforward-first?
- In on-prem environments rollbacks are often brittle due to stateful components, database migrations, and long reconciliation loops.
- Rollforward (progressive traffic migration + quick fixes) reduces blast radius and makes forward-compatible fixes the default path.
- Combined with short-lived canaries and automated safeguards, rollforward gives better availability for customer infra.

High level pipeline sketch (CI -> CD):
1) PR opens against infra repo (terraform modules) OR k8s-app repo (helm chart + values).
2) CI validates: static lint, unit tests, terraform plan (if TF changes), helm lint + chart tests, container build, cosign sign + attestation creation.
3) CI publishes artifact and creates an image provenance entry in SLSA datastore (we use simple internal index + cosign attestations).
4) Merge triggers GitOps commit to cluster repo (applications/ apps/<env>/team-app.yaml) with a canary overlay.
5) ArgoCD picks up the change, deploys canary (5-10% traffic or single replica depending on service), health checks run for N minutes.
6) If health gates pass, automated promotion increments traffic in waves until full rollforward. If a gate fails, a fast rollback to previous app revision is possible but flagged for human review.

Preflight checks (CI):
- Terraform: terraform fmt, validate, plan with -out and upload plan artifact. If module major version bump detected require manual approval.
- Helm: helm lint, kubeconform or chart-testing, dry-run against target k8s version.
- Container images: run unit/integration tests, SBOM generation, cosign sign, and cosign verify step in pipeline producing verification metadata artifact.
- Secrets & config: verify that any new secret references map to secrets manager (Vault/KMS) entries and that argocd-sealed-secrets or ExternalSecrets manifests are present.

Argo/GitOps patterns (canary -> rollforward):
- Use a canary overlay per environment under apps/<env>/<app>-canary.yaml that sets replica/weights and additional debug annotations.
- Argo sync waves: define sequential sync waves to ensure CRD/controller reconciliations happen in order (e.g., pre-hook: validate CRDs -> sync main controllers -> sync kustomize overlays -> post-sync checks).
- Health hooks: use Argo resource hooks for smoke-tests and hit the readiness endpoints. If a hook fails, Argo auto-rollbacks the app to previous live revision.
- Promotion controller (lightweight job): a GitHub Action/Argo Rollout job monitors canary metrics (error rate, p95 latency) and creates a follow-up commit to remove the canary overlay, effectively promoting the release.

Rollforward strategy (detailed):
- Stage 0 (canary): 1 replica or 5% traffic, run 15-20m health window, collect metrics from Prometheus and application logs.
- Stage 1 (scaled canary): 25% traffic, 10m window.
content_continued:
- Stage 2 (wide canary): 50% traffic, 5-10m window.
- Stage 3 (rollforward): 100% traffic unless a guard trips.
- Immediate fix path: if a critical regression is detected at any stage, teams can push a hotfix image tagged with same provenance; the promotion job recognizes a 'hotfix' commit and restarts the promotion from the current stage rather than full rollback.

Image signing + provenance (CI details):
- Build step: docker build -> create SBOM (syft) -> cosign sign (private key stored in KMS via auth plugin) -> upload signature and attestation to artifact registry.
- Verification step in Argo: argocd plugin runs cosign verify on image referenced in the manifest. If cosign verification fails, the app remains in Pending/Suspended state and an alert is fired.
- Attestation model: include fields: git_sha, builder_job_id, sbom_link, terraform_plan_id (if infra change), and list of checksums. Use Predicate format consistent with SLSA 1/2.

Terraform module notes and versioning:
- Module layout: modules/vpc, modules/k8s-cluster, modules/networking, modules/iam. Each module has changelog.md and migration.md.
- Versioning policy: semantic versioning with special rules: patch = safe changes, minor = additive changes, major = breaking (migration required). CI blocks automatic module updates if major change occurs.
- Recommended usage pattern in environment repos: pin module source to a tag (git::https://...//modules/vpc?ref=v1.4.2) and keep a central modules-lock.tf file in infra-ops to track approved versions.
- Module testing: use terratest GH Action for modules on PRs against modules/* and run integration plan/apply in ephemeral sandbox (GCP/AWS dev project or on-prem VM testbed).

Kubernetes/Helm upgrade mechanics:
- Charts are packaged with exact app image tags (not :latest). Values.yaml for canary overlay must include trafficWeight (for Istio/Contour) or replicaCount overrides.
- For stateful workloads: create a migration plan entry in the release PR and tag DB schema changes distinctly. If a migration is required, the release must include a migration job artifact that can be run by SRE during maintenance window.
- Helm hooks: avoid heavy pre-upgrade hooks; prefer separate migration jobs to reduce upgrade coupling.

Secrets and keys:
- Image cosign signing keys: private key material never committed. Use KMS-backed signer service (KMS + ephemeral signing context) or a short-lived signing container that fetches key material from HSM.
- ArgoCD and GitOps credentials: use read-only deploy keys for repo access, and restrict the ArgoCD service account to target namespace RBAC.
- KMS rotation notes: rotation must be announced in infra-ops channel and new key used for signing with backward compatibility: verify signatures made by older keys remain valid for a cooldown period.

Monitoring and gates:
- Primary gates: 5xx error rate, p95 latency, request success ratio.
- Observability required for canary: traces (sampled), metrics (per-endpoint), logs (structured). Canary promotion job requires gating rules expressed as a simple JSON/DSL file checked into repo (e.g., gates.json).
- Auto-fail behavior: if gate fails during stage, mark deployment with a critical alert and either: 1) pause promotion for human triage, or 2) auto-rollback to previous live revision depending on severity threshold.

Runbook snippets (on-call):
- Fast-fail scenario (high error rate after canary): 1) pause promotion job, 2) scale canary to zero if immediate mitigation needed, 3) open a P0 incident and notify Product and Customer Success, 4) look at cosign attestations to confirm correct image was deployed.
- Hotfix path: build new image, sign, update canary overlay with hotfix tag, re-run promotion checks. This avoids full rollback and keeps state changes forward moving.

Operational checklist before merging a release to private repo:
- [ ] Terraform plan uploaded and non-blocking OR approved manual signoff for major changes.
- [ ] Helm lint + dry-run passes.
- [ ] Cosign signature present and verified in CI.
- [ ] Gates file present and configured for target env.
- [ ] Observatory dashboards created/updated for new endpoints.
- [ ] Migration plan present if DB/schema changes included.

Example GitHub Actions snippets (conceptual):
- name: Build and attest image
  run: |
    docker build -t registry.internal/repo/app:${{ github.sha }} .
    syft packages -o json > sbom.json
    cosign sign --key k8s://projects/myproj/locations/global/keyRings/kr/cryptoKeys/k --output-signature sig --output-attestation attestation.json registry.internal/repo/app:${{ github.sha }}

- name: Upload artifact to provenance index
  run: |
    curl -X POST -H "Content-Type: application/json" --data-binary @attestation.json https://provenance.internal/api/v1/attestations

Notes on testing and local dev:
- Provide a lightweight local mode in dev with a small k3s cluster + an argocd instance to iterate on overlays. Use a mock cosign verifier that accepts test-key for local testing.

Security considerations: 
- Attestations must be tamper-evident. Keep a read-only mirror of attestations in an immutable storage bucket for audits.
- Access to deploy keys & KMS should be limited via short-lived tokens and just-in-time approval for high-sensitivity repo merges.

Unresolved questions / things to decide:
- Do we require mandatory SLSA attestation on every image for private clusters or allow exception for local-only patches? (Action: security to propose policy)
- Should major Terraform module upgrades be gated by a special 'infra-ops' approver list? (Action: infra-ops to draft a policy)
- How long do we continue to accept signatures made by rotated keys? Define a rotation grace period. (Action: security + infra)

Action items and owners:
- Marcus Lee: prototype a promotion controller that reads gates.json and performs commits to app repo (target: 2026-03-01).
- Sofia Ramirez: write migration guidelines for stateful sets and DB-backed services (target: 2025-11-01).
- Ethan Park: add cosign verification plugin for ArgoCD in the argocd-dev repo and run load test (target: 2026-01-15).

References and inspiration:
- Sigstore / Cosign docs, SLSA provenance guides, Argo Rollouts patterns, and GitOps best practices.

Notes to self (loose thoughts):
- Consider storing the gates.json schema as a CRD eventually so Argo can validate it natively.
- For on-prem air-gapped clusters we need an offline attestation relay that can accept cosign signatures pushed from CI and hold them until cluster syncs.

This is a working doc — expect lots of follow-ups and iterations.
